h: פָּרָשַׁת פָּרָה, מַאֲמָר ג׳ Parshas Parah — Maamar Gimmel

p: "Who can bring the pure out of the impure?
Yisrael from the nations of the world;
the World to Come from this world.
the Unique One of the world?"
That is, so it arose in Thought,
in which "And He said" is not stated,
the intellect hidden from all thought;
which allude to the deeds of the wicked.
For thus was the creation of the world:
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קפד, א)
And this is what they said, "the World to Come,"
that was hidden away for the future to come,
and it will be revealed out of this world —
light that emerges from within darkness.
And as for what they said, "Yisrael from the nations,"
that they came from Terach and his forebears,
for about that it already said
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים פז, ב)
in line with what they said (Pesachim 87b):
except so that converts would be added to them."
And they, of blessed memory, explained
that the intent is not to actual converts
and vitality that are in the nations,
בְּסוֹד וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כּוּלָּם [נְחֶמְיָה ט, ו]
in the secret of "And You give life to them all" (Nechemiah 9:6);
and this is extracted through the exiles.
And for this reason it says
on the pasuk "The voice of my Beloved,
הִנֵּה זֶה בָּא [שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב, ח]
לֹא כְּבָר נִשְׁבַּע הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
Did not HaKadosh Baruch Hu already swear
That is, all of them have in them
and for this the exiles were needed
among all seventy nations of the world.
וְעַל זֶה מְשִׁיבָן אֶחָד גּוֹלֶה לְבַרְבַּרְיָא כּוּ׳
And to this He answers them: "One is exiled to Barbaria, etc. —
it is as though you were all exiled";
And this is what they said,
Is it not the Unique One of the world?"
For so the Name Havayah One indicates,
that He is One since the world was created
just as before it was created;
for although it appears after Creation
that there are minds and free choice,
it is all from Hashem Yisbarach,
just as before the world was created.
And when this light shines forth in the heart,
then it is a repair for all the blemish
And this is the matter of the Parah,
which purifies even from the tumah of a corpse,
since it is the purification of Yisrael
from the tumah of the yetzer hara,
that is, Hashem Yisbarach will make clear
that so it arose in Thought before Him,
and willful sins will be like merits,
when there is a revelation of Atika,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג עט, ב)
the time of the meal of Atika,
a semblance of the World to Come,
which is from the light hidden away for the World to Come.
וְעַל כֵּן קוֹרִין אָז פָּרָשַׁת פָּרָה
And therefore Parshas Parah is read then,
for it points to this light,

paragraphs.text: Job 14:4 — “Who can bring a pure thing from an impure one? Not one.” The Midrash turns the question into an affirmation: Is it not the One—the Unique One of the world—who can bring purity from impurity?

paragraphs.text: Bamidbar Rabbah 19:1 — “‘Who can bring a pure thing from an impure one? Is it not the One?’ Such as Abraham from Terach, Hezekiah from Ahaz, Josiah from Amon, Mordechai from Shimei, Israel from the nations, and the World to Come from this world. Who did this? Who commanded this? Who decreed this? Is it not the Unique One of the world?”

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 77b — “He said to him: ‘Why do the goats go first, and afterward the sheep?’ He answered: ‘Like the creation of the world: first darkness, and afterward light.’” Rabbi Zeira’s question to Rav Yehudah supplies the expression quoted here. Rav Tzadok applies the sequence of darkness and light to the purification that brings the future world out of the present one.

paragraphs.text: Pesachim 87b — “Rabbi Elazar said: The Holy One, blessed be He, exiled Israel among the nations only so that converts might be added to them, as it says, ‘I shall sow her for Myself in the land.’ Does a person sow a se’ah except to bring in many kor?” The Gemara expressly speaks of converts and compares exile with sowing. The extension to holy sparks within the nations belongs to the mystical explanation cited by Rav Tzadok.

paragraphs.text: Shaar HaPesukim, Shemot, opening account of the Egyptian exile — “The reason for the exile in which Israel was exiled among the nations has already been explained in the passage of Re’eh, concerning the commandment to remember the Exodus. We said that Adam contained all the souls and all the worlds. When he sinned, all those souls fell from him into the husks, which are divided among the seventy nations. Israel must be exiled there, among each and every nation, to gather the roses of the holy souls scattered among those thorns. As our Sages said in Midrash Rabbah: Why was Israel exiled among the nations? So that converts might be added to them. Understand this well.” The Lurianic text explicitly applies the teaching about added converts to gathering holy souls dispersed among the seventy nations. Rav Tzadok expresses that gathering here in the language of holy sparks and their divine life.

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:8 — “‘The voice of my beloved—behold, he comes’: this is the King Messiah. When he says to Israel, ‘In this month you will be redeemed,’ they say: ‘How can we be redeemed? Has not the Holy One sworn that He will subject us to seventy nations?’ He says: ‘One of you goes into exile to Barbaria, and one to Samatria; it is as though all of you had gone into exile.’” This is the passage cited in the manuscript as Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:22; the retrieved edition places it within 2:8. The interpretation of these dispersed exiles as the collection of holy sparks is Rav Tzadok’s development.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim (Radzin), Parshas Parah 4 — “To see purity in the very garment that before seemed the opposite… is possible only when it shines from the highest place, called ‘One,’ the will stripped of all garments.” Like Rav Tzadok, the Radziner reads “Is it not the One” as the level above choice and its garments. There purity shows itself within the impure thing itself, with nothing changed.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Masei 11 — “Already in the first utterance darkness and the deeds of the wicked are mentioned… and willful sins become merits, when it is made clear that it was all only so that it be ‘very good.’” Rav Tzadok there adds a warning. The yetzer hara uses this very truth to coax a person to sin, as Bilaam smoothed Yisrael’s path to Shittim. The clarification comes only through teshuvah.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 79b (Achrei Mot) — “‘From new moon to new moon and from Sabbath to Sabbath’: why is one equated with the other? ... Their joy in one another is found only when Atika Kadisha is revealed, and then there is joy for all.... Of ‘A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day,’ we learned: for the Sabbath day itself—the praise with which the Holy One, blessed be He, praises it. Then joy is found, and the soul is increased, for Atika is revealed and union is made ready.” The quoted passage establishes the revelation of Atika and the additional soul on Sabbath. Rav Tzadok specifies the morning meal here in applying that revelation to the reading of Parah.
